faqs.q: What is an AI browser agent?
faqs.a: An AI that uses a real web browser to do a job: it opens pages, reads them, clicks and fills in forms, deciding each step as it goes. It is for websites that have no app or API to connect to. [Browser automation without code](/guides/browser-automation-without-code) compares the kinds.

faqs.q: Can it log in to websites?
faqs.a: Yes, with you. When a site needs a sign-in, it asks in Needs you and you sign in yourself in its browser; a password never goes into a chat. The sign-in stays in its browser for later runs.
No, never. It tries another source first; if one site is the only way, it asks you to solve the check yourself in its browser, or to leave that site out.

faqs.q: Is a browser agent the same as web scraping?
faqs.a: Close, but not the same. A scraper pulls set fields from many pages; a browser agent reads a few pages, understands them and tells you what matters, such as [which competitor price changed](/guides/how-to-monitor-competitor-prices-automatically). For scraping many rows into a table, a tool like Browse AI fits better.

faqs.q: When should I not use a browser agent?
faqs.a: When the site has an app in the catalog. An app connection reads the data directly, with no pages to load or change under it, so Captain builds an automation or an AI agent there.

Yes, when its instructions say so. It fills the form from what you give it, then stops and asks you in Needs you before it submits. [How to automate form filling on websites](/guides/how-to-automate-form-filling-on-websites) shows the steps.
